description: The list of vague-token triggers. Each entry is a token or regex pattern that, when found in scanned text, is a candidate red-flag for an AI-stretch. Triggers may carry per-token exempt-context cues that suppress the flag when the surrounding text shows the token is being used in its precise sense. Triggers are not banned vocabulary; they are detection points whose diagnostic injects nearby glossary context. The list grows as new stretches surface.

triggers.reason: Vague stand-in for a specific named group (the 561 Group, the RSC Quiescent, the tiyóšpaye, a Lakota band, etc.). The precise name is almost always available nearby.

Stand-in for an unspecified implementation/byte-layer. The repo has precise vocabulary: posix-file, cell, predication-cell, kernel cell log, Node ESM module, the predicated-computing implementation it cites.

Used loosely as a buzzword for 'directory' or 'top-level thing'. Apex means apex of a cone in category theory — the initial algebra of a closure operator, the structure-side fixed point. Flag suppressed when the precise category-theory reading is adjacent.
Filler — 'in order to' / 'in order for' add nothing over 'to' / 'so' / 'for'. Each occurrence is a candidate for deletion.
Vague stand-in. Use the specific scheme (Diátaxis is a four-mode taxonomy, the apex tower is a CHL recursion, Nix is a build tool).
Vague stand-in. Use the specific operation (closure-rule firing, hook dispatch, MCP-server registration, schema validation, witness emission).
Vague stand-in. Use the specific set of named components.
Vague stand-in. Use the specific named component (the Nix flake, the hook config, the witness log, the cell log).
Vague stand-in. Use the specific verb-phrase (the closure firing; the schema validation; the per-day witness log).
Filler. 'X is essentially Y' is either 'X is Y' (drop 'essentially') or 'X approximates Y' (say so precisely).
Filler. Same shape as essentially — either the claim is direct or it is approximated; name which.
Performative adjective with no referent. Drop or replace with the property that justified the word.

hedgePatterns.reason: The 'in the X sense' hedge reframes a precise term as bespoke. If the term means X precisely, just say so. If it does not, do not use the term.
False specificity. The precise referent is named in the records; reference it directly.
Hedge that frames a term as having a special local meaning. If the term means its standard thing, say so without 'means here'. If it does not, use a different term.
Hedge that reframes a precise term as project-bespoke. Same diagnosis as above.
